newsitem.title: UK: IGC cuts 1996 world wheat crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: IGC cuts 1996 world wheat crop estimate.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday cut its estimate for the world's 1996 wheat crop to 580 million tonnes from its previous estimate a month ago of 581 million.

In its Grain Market Report, the IGC saw a sharper fall for CIS output at 63.3 million tonnes from the previous 64 million, compared with 59.0 million in 1995. This difference stems from a million tonne cut in estimated Kazakhstan production, partially offset by rises in smaller CIS states.

Among other changes to 1996 estimates were cuts in Italian output, seen at 7.9 million tonnes from 8.4 a month ago. Mexican production was cut by 200,000 tonnes to three million. Turkey's estimated production was cut by 300,000 tonnes to 16.2 million and that of Pakistan by 100,000 tonnes to 16.9 million.
There were some rises to offset the cuts. An extra 100,000 tonnes was added to the estimate for French production, bringing it to 35.9 million tonnes compared with a 1995 figure of 30.9 million.

The IGC also upped its Polish production estimate by 100,000 tonnes to 8.5 million and for Chile by 100,000 tonnes to 1.5 million. Estimated South African production was raised by 400,000 tonnes to 5.9 million.
